package in.otrail;

import static org.junit.Assert.*;

import org.json.JSONObject;
import org.junit.Test;

public class UpdateManifestTest {
  private JSONObject valid() throws Exception {
    return new JSONObject()
        .put("versionCode", 7)
        .put("versionName", "0.2.5")
        .put("apkUrl", UpdateManifest.PREFIX + "oTraiL-0.2.5-debug.apk")
        .put("sha256", "a".repeat(64))
        .put("sizeBytes", 4_500_000);
  }

  @Test
  public void comparesVersionCodesNotStrings() throws Exception {
    UpdateManifest m = UpdateManifest.parse(valid().toString());
    assertTrue(m.newerThan(6));
    assertFalse(m.newerThan(7));
    assertFalse(m.newerThan(8));
  }

  @Test
  public void rejectsForeignArtifacts() throws Exception {
    for (String url :
        new String[] {
          "http://raw.githubusercontent.com/viskie/oTrail0/main/releases/a.apk",
          "https://evil.example/a.apk",
          UpdateManifest.PREFIX + "../a.apk",
          UpdateManifest.PREFIX + "a.apk?token=x"
        })
      try {
        UpdateManifest.parse(valid().put("apkUrl", url).toString());
        fail(url);
      } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
      }
  }

  @Test
  public void rejectsBadDigestAndOversizedDownload() throws Exception {
    try {
      UpdateManifest.parse(valid().put("sha256", "not-a-checksum").toString());
      fail();
    } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
    }
    try {
      UpdateManifest.parse(valid().put("sizeBytes", 100_000_000).toString());
      fail();
    } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
    }
  }
}

FILE: docs/0.2.3-changes.md
================================================================================

# oTraiL 0.2.3 — implementation and upgrade guide

This update implements the supplied stop-geocoding guide and the additional requests for nearby historic places, sequential marker popups, the entire collected trail, and coloured gap connections. It keeps inferred connections in logs only, with no estimate label on the map and no fabricated GPS fixes.

## 1. Safeguard the existing journal

Before modifying source, the existing commit was preserved as branch `backup-before-stop-geocoding`; the original Java directory was copied outside the repository. The user's untracked `android-project-sources.txt` is not part of the change.

A raw pre-upgrade archive of the installed app's database, WAL, and preferences was saved on the phone at `Download/oTraiL/pre-geocoding-backup-2026-11-05.tar` (refreshed immediately before deployment; the November 4 archive is also retained). The initial capture checked that database/WAL hashes stayed unchanged during copying. This is an emergency developer archive, **not** a JSON file for the app's Restore button. Normal Google Drive/Files snapshots remain the supported in-app restore format. Do not uninstall to upgrade.

Migration and backup tests are run in an independently installed `in.otrail.validation` application before upgrading `in.otrail`. Test databases are also isolated in device-protected storage; production continues collecting GPS during validation.

## 2. `app/src/main/java/in/otrail/TrailDb.java`

1. Advance SQLite helper version from 1 to 2. Keep `trails.db`, application identity, old tables, IDs and units.
2. Fresh databases add `place_name`, `locality`, `district`, `state`, `country`, `postal_code`, `road`, `geocode_status` (default `PENDING`) and `geocode_attempt_ms` (default 0) to stops.
3. Upgrade v1 using `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` only for stop records. No table is dropped or journal row rewritten. Compare trip/fix/stop counts before/after and append a migration audit to logs.
4. Index the geocoding queue; add an index on global fix time and a derived historic-place cache. A partial unique log index prevents duplicate inferred-gap log entries.
5. Expose stable stop IDs and address/status fields through `Stop`. `stopById` reads one stop directly instead of loading a trip.
6. Return `-1` from `record` for ordinary fixes and the inserted stop ID when a new >2-minute stop is confirmed. StopDetector behavior is unchanged.
7. Add `pendingStopIds`, `saveStopAddress` and `markGeocodeFailed`. Failed lookups are eligible again after 24 hours. Failed/in-flight lookups cannot overwrite an already-resolved address.
8. `fixes(-1)` and `stops(-1)` return all collected journeys chronologically. A selected positive trip ID still filters one journey.
9. Store display-inference details in deduplicated `sync_logs` entries. Never insert inferred samples into `fixes` or change measured coordinates/timestamps.
10. Extend GeoJSON stop properties with stable ID and address/status fields; fix export and `[longitude, latitude]` ordering remain intact. Export `schema_version` remains 1 with additive optional fields.
11. Snapshots already serialize all stop columns. Backup format version stays 1; old backups omit the new columns and receive database defaults. Duplicate-stop restore fills only missing address fields, preserves existing names and timings, and may promote an unresolved stop to `RESOLVED`. Existing transactional rollback and trip-ID remapping remain.

## 3. `app/src/main/java/in/otrail/StopGeocoder.java` — new

1. Keep a single throttled coordinator independent of UI, GPS writing, cloud backup and historic-site fetching.
2. Read eligible stops from SQLite; resolve one at a time, about one per second plus lookup time. Continue draining historical stops beyond the first batch; coalesce repeated backfill requests.
3. Use Android Geocoder's asynchronous API on API 33+. Wait at most 15 seconds on this background worker.
4. On API 30–32, contain the synchronous call in a bounded single-thread executor with a 15-second wait. If a legacy binder call ignores interruption, it occupies at most that one legacy thread rather than spawning replacements indefinitely.
5. Save place/locality/district/state/country/PIN/road when available. Null/empty responses, unavailable services, errors and timeouts become `FAILED`; coordinates are unchanged.
6. Never hold a SQLite transaction open across a lookup. Empty Address objects are not incorrectly marked resolved.

Android's Geocoder may be absent, inaccurate, incomplete or network-dependent. There is no embedded offline address database. See [Android Geocoder](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/location/Geocoder).

## 4. `app/src/main/java/in/otrail/TrackingService.java`

1. Backfill at initial service startup and wake eligible retries hourly; newly confirmed stop IDs also wake the queue.
2. Move GPS writes onto a dedicated serial executor so a cloud backup upload cannot occupy the GPS writer. Geocoding uses its own executor.
3. Keep the 5,000 ms GPS request, zero minimum distance, GPS provider, persistent notification, permission checks, START_STICKY and reboot/update recovery.
4. Shut down workers in order and close their shared database only after queued GPS/backup work finishes.

Geocoding has no path that stops the service or ends a journey. Location delivery still depends on Android, permissions and GPS reception.

## 5. `app/src/main/java/in/otrail/MainActivity.java`

1. Load the entire journal for the default Live view; History offers “Entire collected trail” and individual journeys.
2. Fit the initial viewport to the entire collected trail. Locate returns to the current position and can request a fresh fix even while recording.
3. Render stop popup title from place name, with locality, road, district, state, country, PIN, arrival, observed duration, departure/last observation and coordinates. Unresolved locations remain selectable.
4. Include all Stop record fields in the display signature. An address update refreshes the marker even without a new GPS fix.
5. Use stable marker keys; close the previous popup before binding a clicked marker. Preserve the selected popup across periodic redraws and close it on a blank-map tap.
6. Draw gap connections in amber with no text label or inference popup, as requested. Keep the inference details only in logs.
7. Add “Identify historical stop locations” in Maps & downloads. It respects the 24-hour failure cooldown.
8. Add “Old places” with find/refresh, cached display and hide options. Search uses a recent GPS position within India and a 25 km radius, not an arbitrary map pan position. The offline-only switch blocks refresh but permits cached results.
9. Show up to 50 nearest matching places as gold name labels on every basemap; popup includes source date, age range/approximation when present in the source, cache time and an OSM source link. Historic-place age descriptions are separate from trail-gap rendering.
10. Send historic network requests on their own executor so they do not delay GPS writing or map refresh.

## 6. `app/src/main/java/in/otrail/MarkerPopups.java` — new

Centralize the one-popup-at-a-time policy so it can be exercised directly by a device regression test, including A → B → A clicks. The activity manages stable ownership across map redraws.

## 7. `app/src/main/java/in/otrail/TrailSegments.java` — new

1. Consume recorded samples in chronological order, across all journeys.
2. Keep observed runs separate at a recording gap or journey boundary. Preserve the first/last sample of every run when thinning displayed points.
3. Add a separate straight-line display edge only for gaps of at most 30 minutes, at most 60 km, and plausible implied speed at most 60 m/s. Long or implausible gaps stay disconnected.
4. Keep the recorded and inferred edge types separate. Only the renderer uses the amber edges; export and backups contain measured GPS points, not a guessed route.

This does not infer the road taken or perform map matching. There is insufficient evidence to recreate a driven route from two endpoints alone.

## 8. `app/src/main/java/in/otrail/HistoricAge.java` — new

Parse OSM year/date values, explicitly approximate years, century tags and closed year ranges. At the current UTC year, accept only source date ranges wholly within the requested 200–600 year age window. Unknown dates, open-ended dates and unsupported expressions are not assigned an invented age.

## 9. `app/src/main/java/in/otrail/HistoricPlaces.java` — new

1. Request named historic/heritage/tourism elements with `start_date` from the public Overpass service, on demand, within 25 km of the phone's recent fix.
2. Enforce India bounds, request/read timeouts, a 300-element query cap and a 4 MB response cap. Reject partial/error responses while retaining existing cache.
3. Normalize source type/ID, name, coordinates, original date, year range, uncertainty and fetch time into SQLite.
4. Filter by source date and actual distance. Return nearest cached sites offline; no geocoding or GPS dependency for reading the cache.

Coverage depends on OSM tags and public server availability. Age tags are not independently authenticated; an empty result means no matching dated data was returned, not that no old places exist. Map data/caches stay on the phone. See [OSM start_date](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Key:start_date) and [Overpass query language](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API/Overpass_QL).

## 10. Tests

`app/src/androidTest/java/in/otrail/BackupInstrumentation.java` has 14 checks:

1. Upgrade a genuine v1 database while preserving IDs, coordinates, timestamps, foreign keys and logs.
2. Restore a v1 JSON backup with default pending address fields.
3. Preserve addresses in snapshots.
4. Include addresses and correct coordinate order in GeoJSON.
5. Roll back a truncated snapshot.
6. Restore enriched stop fields.
7. Merge enrichment into unresolved duplicates without duplicating GPS rows.
8. Preserve an existing name while filling missing address fields.
9. Confirm stop ID return and allow GPS writes during a deliberately blocked lookup.
10. Handle lookup failure and enforce/release the 24-hour cooldown.
11. Drain more than 25 historical stops.
12. Filter/cache historic source dates and reject distant results.
13. Record inferred edges only once in logs, without adding GPS fixes.
14. Open popups A → B → A with only the selected marker's window open.

`TrailSegmentsTest.java` adds four JVM tests for endpoint retention, short-gap connections, implausible/long-gap rejection and journey separation. `HistoricAgeTest.java` adds four date/age parsing tests. The six existing StopDetector tests remain unchanged: 14 JVM tests total. Tests use fake addresses, never a live geocoder response.

## 11. `app/build.gradle`

Keep normal application ID `in.otrail`, SDK 30/35 and dependencies. Increment to versionCode 5 / versionName 0.2.3. The `-PvalidationBuild` switch changes only the validation installation ID to `in.otrail.validation`, preventing test upgrades from touching production data.

## 12. Build and upgrade sequence

```sh
. /src/android-build-env/environment.sh
./gradlew -PvalidationBuild testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug assembleDebugAndroidTest
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/androidTest/debug/app-debug-androidTest.apk
adb shell am instrument -w in.otrail.validation.test/in.otrail.BackupInstrumentation

# Only after validation succeeds, build the real application:
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
adb shell am start -n in.otrail/.MainActivity
```

The real update uses the existing debug signing identity and `adb install -r`. No uninstall, data clear, map deletion or permission reset is part of deployment. APK snapshots and checksums go in the repository's `releases/` folder, not GitHub Releases. Live geocoder/provider availability and long-duration battery behavior remain distinct from deterministic automated checks.

FILE: docs/0.2.4-navigation-updates.md

# 0.2.4 — silent in-app navigation and repository updates

## Use navigation

1. Install the new APK **over** the existing app, retaining its package/signing identity and all app storage. Do not uninstall. Trail database schema remains version 2; no migration, deletion, or rewrite is introduced.
2. Tap **Navigate**, enter a place name or `latitude, longitude`, explicitly search and choose a result. Alternatively hold a location on the map and select **Preview in oTraiL**.
3. A recent, reasonably accurate GPS fix is required as the starting point. If necessary tap Locate and wait for reception. Destinations are limited approximately to India.
4. Review the blue route, total driving distance and duration, then tap **Start**. The panel shows written maneuvers, distance to the next instruction, remaining distance and approximate remaining time. There is **no voice guidance**, speech engine or sound alert.
5. Recenter resumes following the live GPS dot after panning. Turns opens the complete maneuver list. Clear ends navigation and clears the route cache; GPS journaling keeps running.

The default route provider is the FOSSGIS public OSRM car endpoint. It is suitable for light personal use and has no availability guarantee or live traffic. Request origin/destination are sent to the selected routing server. Search uses Android's geocoder, which may be absent or network-dependent; map-point and coordinate entry are alternatives. Maps & downloads allows a replacement HTTPS OSRM driving endpoint.

Sources: [OSRM API](https://project-osrm.org/docs/v5.24.0/api/), [FOSSGIS routing usage/privacy](https://routing.openstreetmap.de/about.html). The app identifies itself, displays routing attribution, links to map corrections, spaces manual requests by at least two seconds and automatic reroutes by at least 60 seconds.

## Guidance, offline behavior and data integrity

- Navigation geometry/steps are derived data in `navigation-route.json`, written atomically on a separate worker. They are never appended to `fixes`, substituted for measurements, or mixed into stop/GeoJSON exports.
- GPS recording stays on its existing dedicated writer. Navigation receives a copy after the real fix is committed. Guidance calculation, route HTTP requests and cache writes use independent workers.
- Fresh GPS fixes update route progress. Inaccurate and duplicate fixes are ignored for navigation. Rerouting requires three accurate off-route observations and a cooldown. Arrival requires repeated good fixes near the route end and proximity to the requested target.
- A failed reroute keeps the cached route; a failed replacement preview retains the previous route/target consistently. The user sees the failure. Stale GPS is shown rather than pretending current guidance.
- Active/preview routes restore from cache across app/process/reboot restarts. Offline-only blocks new route calculations and reroutes. The existing cached geometry and turn list can still be followed with GPS.
- This is **not a full offline routing engine**. It cannot calculate a new path when disconnected. Existing `.map` files render maps, while `.osm.pbf` is raw source data; neither is directly a navigable graph here.
- Full collected trails, stop enrichment, inferred-gap logs, map downloads and trail backups remain separate. There is no database-version change for this release.

## Daily and manual GitHub updates

Maps & downloads → **App updates · daily / check now** enables/disables daily checks and provides Check now. Daily checks are enabled by default, network-constrained, persisted with Android JobScheduler and quiet when there is no newer version. Android may defer periodic jobs; it is not an exact wall-clock alarm. Newer versions produce one notification per version when notification permission is granted. Background checks never download/install an APK silently.

The update source is `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/viskie/oTrail0/main/releases/latest.json`. No GitHub Releases API, account token, or GitHub Release publishing workflow is used.

The manifest contains:

```json
{
  "versionCode": 6,
  "versionName": "0.2.4",
  "apkUrl": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/viskie/oTrail0/main/releases/oTraiL-0.2.4-debug.apk",
  "sha256": "<generated from the exact APK>",
  "sizeBytes": 0,
  "notes": "Release notes"
}
```

The example digest/size above are illustrative; the actual committed manifest has the real values. For every future APK:

1. Increment Android versionCode/versionName and build with the **same signing key**.
2. Commit the APK in `releases/`.
3. Generate its SHA-256 and size and update `releases/latest.json` and `releases/SHA256SUMS` in the same commit.
4. Push to main; the next daily or manual check can see it. Raw GitHub responses may be cached briefly.

The app accepts only HTTPS artifact URLs in this repository's releases directory, enforces a size limit and checks the full SHA-256. Before sharing a private read-only APK URI with Android's installer it verifies package name, exact advertised version, strictly higher versionCode and the same APK signing certificate set as the installed app. Failed candidates are not installed. The verified artifact is separate from journals and map storage. No uninstall/data-clear operation exists in this updater.

The first install may require **Allow from this source** for oTraiL. Android still requires the user's install confirmation; ordinary apps cannot silently replace themselves. See [Android install-source permission](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/content/pm/PackageManager#canRequestPackageInstalls()). Debug signing is still for personal testing; preserve the signing identity for future updates.

## Validation for this release

- 29 JVM tests: existing stop, geometry and heritage tests plus route parsing, written maneuvers, progress/arrival, off-route confirmation, duplicate/poor-accuracy rejection, loop handling, immutable geometry and update-manifest restrictions/version comparisons.
- Android lint and debug app/test APK compilation.
- A live synthetic Delhi routing request returned 244 geometry points and 20 maneuvers; the app's production parser read it successfully.
- An additional device instrumentation check compares journal snapshots before/after cached-navigation operations. It is compiled here, **not executed for 0.2.4**, because the phone is unavailable; the requested delivery is an APK upload to GitHub. Phone UI, actual driving, and the Android installer flow still need device testing.
- Previous 0.2.3 device checks are not presented as new 0.2.4 device validation.

## Suggested offline routing techniques (next phase)

1. **Route caching — implemented now.** Cache a planned route and its instructions. This covers loss of connectivity while staying on that route, but cannot calculate detours.
2. **BRouter on-device graph tiles.** BRouter provides Java/Android offline routing and 5×5-degree `.rd5` graph segments, with configurable profiles including car routing. A regional tile downloader plus an adapter to `RoutePlan` would enable local recalculation. Validate car profiles and maneuver quality against your India journeys. This is the most direct Android-oriented candidate to prototype. [BRouter project and data layout](https://github.com/abrensch/brouter).
3. **Native Valhalla with regional routing tiles.** A longer-term option for a dedicated car-navigation pipeline: build regional graph packs from OSM extracts off-device, deliver versioned tiles to the phone, and connect a native Android/JNI engine to the same guidance model. This requires more native build/distribution work; it is not shipped in 0.2.4. [Valhalla](https://github.com/valhalla/valhalla), [tiled graph design](https://valhalla.github.io/valhalla/concepts/tiles/).

For either graph engine, start with the states/corridors you drive, include boundary overlap, keep graph data out of the APK/repository, and use manual phone downloads with size/progress/checksum/rollback support. Route graphs and recorded GPS trails must remain separate datasets.

# 0.3.0 — repeated passes, distance and road context

## Trail colors

The app keeps a fixed 31-color pass palette, viewable in Maps & downloads. Repeated traversal of the same quantized geographic edges after two minutes receives another color, including reverse traversal. Colors cycle after pass 31. Detection is an approximate 35-metre display grid, not road-network map matching; GPS offsets, parallel lanes and sparse fixes can affect matches. Green is reserved for inferred continuity. Color geometry is derived off the main thread and never edits recorded fixes.

## Distance and drive logs

The main statistics show total recorded kilometres. Selected history also shows its own trail distance. The moving/recording status includes the current drive's recorded kilometres since the most recent stop departure. Stop dots and the Stops list show distance and elapsed average speed since the previous stop, with a gap notice when coverage is incomplete. The first leg starts at the first collected fix.

Distance uses original, unthinned observations. Poor accuracy, impossible speed, long GPS gaps and stationary jitter are excluded; recorded stop intervals do not accumulate parked drift. Green inferred edges are excluded. Average speed is recorded distance divided by elapsed departure-to-arrival time; missing GPS coverage can understate it. No missing route distance is invented.

Database v2 to v3 adds only the derived stop_drive_metrics table. Existing trips, fixes, stop details and sync logs are retained. Metrics backfill all collected history, update in the background and appear as numeric properties on stop GeoJSON features. Normalized trail backups retain the source observations and stop timing; derived metrics are recomputed after restore rather than treated as independent source records. Map/routing datasets and road caches remain outside trail backups.

## Road names and landmarks

Tap a road, including a recorded trail or navigation line, to see its mapped reference/name. Cached results appear first; online refresh is attempted when not in Offline only mode, subject to request throttling. The Turns button still opens navigation instructions.

While moving, the road strip and amber markers show cached landmarks ahead along the identified road, including temples, mosques, churches, gurdwaras, other places of worship, historic sites, attractions and viewpoints. Tap the strip for a list or an amber marker for details. Source data is OpenStreetMap via Overpass; it is not an exhaustive inventory of every public landmark. Unnamed places of worship can appear under their mapped type. Attribution and fetch dates are shown where relevant.

Current-road association uses nearby mapped road geometry and matching reference/name, with a 100-metre roadside corridor and rejection of closer alternative named roads. Ahead filtering uses recent direction of travel. These are proximity estimates, not confirmation of access or opening hours. The downloaded offline basemap itself is not mined for road/POI features.

Road areas are cached in a separate phone-only SQLite database. Automatic lookup reads the cache first, refreshes missing/older-than-seven-day areas online, and limits automatic requests to one per two minutes. Explicit road taps can refresh a cached area, at most once per five seconds. Network failures retain cached content. Offline only makes no road-service requests. No map, road or POI dataset is bundled in the APK/repository.

## Validation

45 JVM tests pass, including prior navigation, updater, GPS dwell and continuity tests. New checks cover historical leg boundaries, gaps, parked jitter, overlapping legacy stops, reverse repeated passes, 31 unique non-green colors, road-ref normalization, same-road temple inclusion and parallel-road exclusion. Android lint has no errors; app and instrumentation APKs compile. Instrumentation adds a v2-to-v3 journal-preservation check and persistent road-cache reopen check. These new device checks have not run because no ADB phone is connected for this build. Existing map teardown and independent stop-detail fixes remain in place. Live Overpass retrieval and the new UI still need phone verification.

Install this update over the existing app with its unchanged signing identity. Do not uninstall to upgrade.

FILE: docs/0.3.2-gps-quality-ui.md
================================================================================

# 0.3.2 — GPS uncertainty and configurable native text

Confirmed stops survive poor accuracy, impossible speed reports at an unchanged position, a single distant fix and a lost signal. Departure requires coherent movement: at least 20 seconds with four precise moving fixes and at least 60 metres of progress, or 90 seconds and 200 metres of coherent progress under reduced accuracy. The original departure observation is retained once movement is confirmed. Genuine movement is tested separately from synthetic GPS drift.

At tracker restart, recent saved fixes are replayed through the detector. Previously split stops can recover their earlier arrival when three stable co-located observations span at least ten seconds. No coordinate rows are removed or changed, and saved stop IDs/labels are retained. Repairs write the previous timestamps and recovery reason to sync_logs. An overlapping open stop at the same place is closed at its last observed time with a SUPERSEDED audit entry; its ID and saved labels remain intact. A short uncertain excursion during an ongoing stop also recovers directly on stable reception. Stops remain provisional through uncertainty; consistent false GPS movement can still resemble genuine travel, so this is conservative filtering rather than a guarantee of physical position.

The live status keeps the retained stop duration visible, shows a weak-GPS note and suppresses unreliable speed. The location dot stays at the stop anchor during uncertainty, and navigation updates wait for trustworthy fixes. The status can use two lines rather than truncating the signal explanation. History and normalized raw fixes remain available.

Native selectors, switches, inputs, dialogs, lists, map popups and attribution now use INK; text helpers honor their explicitly supplied colors. Buttons keep BUTTON_TEXT and BUTTON. Main text accents use ACCENT_TEXT; muted text uses MUTED. Offline city/town labels use CITY_LABEL_*; other map lettering uses MAP_ROAD_LABEL_COLOR, MAP_OTHER_LABEL_COLOR, MAP_TEXT_OUTLINE_COLOR and MAP_TEXT_FONT. The latter two label colors default to INK. Online raster labels are controlled by their providers. Existing manual font/color choices are preserved.

Verification: 52 JVM checks and lint pass; 24 isolated phone checks cover backup/migration/data integrity, shared database concurrency, restart recovery, poor GPS, retained raw fixes and native text styling. Test fixtures use the validation package, separate from the production journal.

The editor uses the :modules process and compiler the :compiler process, separate from the existing GPS recorder. # 0.4.3 — WTF! map camera

The base app adds a persistent `!` toggle to the map's top-right icon bar, independent of installed modules. Enabled uses purple/cyan; disabled uses black/grey. The live GPS dot stays at the map center. Map dragging cannot detach the camera; zoom remains available. Existing navigation route/turn guidance continues without route-preview fitting taking the camera away from the GPS dot. No destination is invented or navigation started without an existing route.

Travel direction is held toward the upper-right along the exact screen vector `(0.8 right, 1 up)`: slope y/x = 1/0.8 and 38.6598° clockwise from screen-up. The conceptual −20° example is not used. The map rotates about the centered dot using `rotation = diagonal bearing − true GPS course`, with short-arc animation. A screen-space north arrow shows true north as it rotates. GPS course is relative to true north, not a magnetic sensor.

Heading changes require a recent moving fix, speed ≥1.5 m/s and accuracy ≤35 m, and are suppressed during an uncertain signal or a confirmed stop. When recorded GPS course is unavailable, displacement is used only within one minute and beyond combined position uncertainty; otherwise the last reliable orientation is held. Mode, heading and zoom survive activity/app restarts. History temporarily suspends the camera and uses north-up; enabling `!` there returns to live tracking. Disabling restores north-up and free map panning.

Colors, label, typography, diagonal, accuracy/speed limits and turn duration are editable under `WTF_*` in UiConfig.java. No database migration, recorded-fix filtering, journal deletion, collector interval or module-data changes. Existing map providers share the same camera behavior. Android device validation is pending because no phone is currently visible to ADB.

Validation: assembleDebug, testDebugUnitTest (78 tests, zero failures) and lintDebug pass. Geometry tests verify the 1/0.8 slope for courses around the compass, short turns crossing north, and rejection of stopped/stale/weak/noisy/gapped observations. # 0.4.9 — Resonations

A compact native player sits directly above the bottom-right total/status panel in landscape and above total statistics in portrait. Files opens Android's multi-select document picker. Choosing a new set replaces the saved playlist; cancelling leaves it intact. The box shows up to three filenames and a fourth “…” line if more were selected. Files can also come from a compatible document provider; local recordings work offline. No audio is packaged into the app or copied into the trail database.

MP3, audio in MP4/M4A, AMR/3GP, AAC, WAV, OGG/Opus and FLAC recordings use Android's installed codecs. A corrupt, inaccessible or unsupported file is skipped; if none can play, the player stops with a visible error rather than retrying indefinitely. MP4 playback uses its audio without opening a video UI. No recording button or microphone permission is added.

Play loops the entire selected list in order, wrapping from last to first; a one-file list repeats that file. Pause retains the track and position. Clear stops audio and removes the playlist references. Persisted document read permissions and a separate `resonations` preference file preserve selection across app restart and normal upgrades. Original files are never deleted. Media playback is a separate user-started foreground service with notification/lock-screen pause controls and audio focus, independent of the GPS recorder. Screen-off playback holds a playback wake lock; a call or competing audio focus pauses it. Selection is remembered after reboot, but playback only starts when requested.

Typography/color tokens and button labels are configurable in UiConfig. No changes to journal schema, stop detection, offline maps, routing or module data.

Android references: https://developer.android.com/media/platform/supported-formats and https://developer.android.com/media/optimize/audio-focus . Actual format support depends on the codec inside the selected container and device support.

Phone absent from ADB: picker interaction, actual audio codecs and screen-off playback are not yet device-verified.

# Journal locking fix

TrailDb handles now share one reference-counted SQLiteOpenHelper/pool per absolute database path. Previously the GPS writer, UI, geocoder and backup could open independent pools against trails.db; Android did not serialize their competing writes inside one pool. Closing a temporary UI handle no longer closes the active tracker's pool. The last handle closes the pool normally, preserving fixture isolation and resource cleanup.

On Android 15+, normalized backup exports use a read-only transaction so they retain a consistent snapshot without reserving the writer. Earlier Android versions retain the existing nonexclusive transaction fallback. Local backup candidate output is buffered. Journal schema, source coordinates, stop timing and restore merge rules are unchanged.

Validation: clean APK build and lint pass; 22 isolated phone instrumentation checks pass, including concurrent writes/reads, handle ownership, exact GPS row counts, integrity_check and a GPS write completing while a backup snapshot remains open. In-place POCO install confirmed. Post-install integrity_check is ok; no pre-update fixes or stop IDs are missing. The current custom palette still has a duplicate color, so the unrelated 31-unique-colors JVM assertion remains a separate configuration issue.

# Edit the UI and build

Edit `app/src/main/java/in/otrail/UiConfig.java`.

- Colors: ARGB `0xAARRGGBB`. `BUTTON` is the background and `BUTTON_TEXT` is the label. Primary text uses `ACCENT_TEXT`, `HEADING`, `SECONDARY`; surfaces use `BACKGROUND` and `SURFACE`.
- Fonts: `BODY_FONT`, `BUTTON_FONT`, `STATUS_FONT`, `MAP_LABEL_FONT` use Android family names, such as `sans-serif`, `sans-serif-condensed`, `sans-serif-medium`, `serif`, or `monospace`.
- Sizes: edit the named `*_SIZE_SP` fields. `TEXT_SCALE` scales general labels; navigation title/instruction/summary and the status have their own sizes. `MAP_LABEL_SIZE_SP` controls app-drawn historic-place labels. `OFFLINE_MAP_TEXT_SCALE` controls offline basemap captions (default 1). The offline tile cache gets a separate identity when this scale changes.
- Trail/map colors: `TRAIL_COLORS` contains all 31 pass colors, `CONTINUITY` controls inferred connections, `NAV_ROUTE_COLOR` controls the route. App marker backgrounds/text have separate `MAP_LABEL_*` tokens. Existing overlay aliases continue to work.
- Copy: `ENGLISH` holds main screen, navigation, settings, road/landmark and dialog labels, including formatted fragments. Keep formatting placeholders such as `%.2f` intact. It does not rename stored database values, source data or routing-engine instructions.
- Languages: `UI_LANGUAGE=""` follows the phone; set `"en"` or `"hi"` to pin it. Add translations to `TRANSLATIONS`, for example `Map.of("hi", Map.of("locate", "मेरी जगह"))`. Missing keys use English. No translations are fabricated or included by default.

Native startup/dialog colors and fonts are generated from the same file during every build; do not edit generated resources. `styles.xml` references those values.

Provider-rendered OSM/Esri raster tiles contain their own road/city typography. Their font, language and color cannot be changed by these UI tokens. Offline Mapsforge uses its zoom-dependent map theme, with density normalized for the fixed tile bridge; app-drawn place labels use the separate UI tokens above.

Build on this workstation:

```bash
cd /src/oTraiL
. /src/android-build-env/environment.sh
./gradlew assembleDebug testDebugUnitTest lintDebug
```

APK: `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`.

Install over the existing app, preserving its data:

```bash
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
```

Do not uninstall or clear storage. Signing keys must match the installed app.

Offline city/town names (e.g. Bilaspur): `CITY_LABEL_FONT`, `CITY_LABEL_STYLE`, `CITY_LABEL_COLOR`, `CITY_LABEL_OUTLINE_COLOR`, `CITY_LABEL_SIZE_SCALE`, `CITY_LABEL_OUTLINE_WIDTH`. Font family values: `default`, `sans_serif`, `serif`, `monospace`. Style values: `normal`, `bold`, `italic`, `bold_italic`. Size scale preserves the underlying zoom visibility rules. Changes automatically use a new tile cache identity. These controls apply to India offline; online raster labels remain provider-controlled.

Dark text: `INK` controls native selectors, switches, inputs, dialog/list text, stop popups and attribution. Main text helpers now honor their explicitly supplied color (`INK`, `MUTED`, etc.). `ACCENT_TEXT` still controls body accents; `HEADING` controls status/headings. Offline road text uses `MAP_ROAD_LABEL_COLOR`, other POI captions use `MAP_OTHER_LABEL_COLOR` (both default to `INK`); their font uses `MAP_TEXT_FONT` and outlines use `MAP_TEXT_OUTLINE_COLOR`. Cities use the independent `CITY_LABEL_*` settings. Provider raster tiles remain unchanged.

Vibrant finish (0.3.4): `VIBRANT_FINISH` enables layered buttons, gradients and colored panel edges. The manually selected `BUTTON` remains the starting color; `BUTTON_GRADIENT_ACCENT` and `BUTTON_GRADIENT_MIX` control its gradient. `BUTTON_EDGE_ACCENT` controls the lower accent edge, and `BUTTON_FONT_STYLE` controls label weight. `PANEL_TINT_MIX` controls panel color strength; `PANEL_ACCENTS` cycles settings card colors. Setting `VIBRANT_FINISH=false` returns flat surfaces/buttons. Base colors, fonts, sizes, map/trail colors and localization choices remain unchanged.

Psychedelic style (0.3.5): `PSYCHEDELIC_GRADIENTS`, `CANVAS_SPECTRUM`, `CANVAS_COLOR_STRENGTH` and `BUTTON_SPECTRUM` control the multi-stop gradients. `BODY_FONT_STYLE`, `BUTTON_FONT_STYLE`, `STATUS_FONT_STYLE`, `HEADING_FONT` and `HEADING_FONT_STYLE` control italics and the playful headings/buttons. City typography now uses four zoom bands, capped by `CITY_LABEL_MIN_SIZE`/`CITY_LABEL_MAX_SIZE`, multiplied by `CITY_LABEL_SIZE_SCALE`. The tile cache identity changes automatically.

Spacing: `BUTTON_INNER_PADDING_DP=4`, `BUTTON_GAP_DP=4`, `CONTROL_ROW_PADDING_DP=2`; sidebar controls use `SIDEBAR_WIDTH_DP=248`, `SIDEBAR_INSET_DP=6`, `PANEL_GAP_DP=4` and `PANEL_INNER_PADDING_DP=6`. Buttons stay 44dp high with centered labels. Button text is now 12sp; the small body/caption/secondary text sizes were increased by one.

Destination text uses `NAV_TITLE_SIZE_SP` (18sp), centered with a two-line limit; turn instructions use `NAV_INSTRUCTION_SIZE_SP` (14sp). Landscape stats stay below the scrolling right-hand controls. `SETTINGS_COLUMNS_LANDSCAPE` controls the three-column settings button rows.

Long stops use `LONG_STOP_MINUTES` (60 minutes), `LONG_STOP_COLOR`, `LONG_STOP_LABEL_SIZE_SP`, `LONG_STOP_LABEL_MIN_ZOOM`, and `LONG_STOP_LABEL_LIMIT`. Big offline city labels use `BIG_CITY_LABEL_COLOR` and `BIG_CITY_LABEL_STYLE`. Long-stop labels become bold italic when their projected screen rectangles overlap a city/town label from the installed offline map. This is an approximate collision check, since the map renderer can displace its labels. Stop-list entries and popups show existing derived inter-stop distance and average speed, including older records.

Map dropdown font: `MAP_SELECTOR_SIZE_SP` (body size +2sp). Total footer: `TOTAL_STATS_TEXT_COLOR` (neon green), `TOTAL_STATS_BACKGROUND` (dark for contrast), `TOTAL_STATS_FONT_STYLE` (bold italic).

Navigation panel: `NAV_PANEL_BACKGROUND` (black), `NAV_TEXT_SPECTRUM` (purple, magenta, violet, cyan, turquoise). Automatic long-stop labels are limited to one and hidden when they collide with another stop label; dots remain tappable.

Navigation heading, instruction and summary now use solid `NAV_TEXT_COLOR` (turquoise), without a text shader. `NAV_TEXT_SPECTRUM` remains available for the panel border/older color references.

Status/Stopped panel uses `STATUS_BACKGROUND` (black), `STATUS_TEXT_COLOR` (cyan), and `STATUS_SPEED_COLOR` (white). The speed span keeps its separate color in every movement state, including unavailable speed.

The floating Locate action shows the application icon inside a hexagon. Edit `LOCATE_SIZE_DP`, `LOCATE_BACKGROUND`, `LOCATE_LOGO_COLOR`, `LOCATE_BORDER_COLOR`, and `LOCATE_RIPPLE_COLOR`; the action and accessibility description remain Locate.

Live status speed uses metres per hour (`0f_m_hr`, m/s ×3600). A known stop always shows zero, even with weak/stale GPS. Uncertain movement remains unknown (`speed_unknown_m_hr`); distances and historical average-speed metrics retain their existing units.

Current live drive uses `LIVE_TRAIL_COLOR` (neon pink); history retains its pass palette and inferred gaps retain green. While stopped, the most recent incoming drive remains highlighted. This changes rendering only. `NAV_TITLE_BOLD` controls the destination's extra bold weight. `LOCATE_VISUAL_SCALE=.60f` reduces the logo and regular hexagon by 40%, while preserving its original touch target; `LOCATE_BEVEL_LIGHT`/`LOCATE_BEVEL_SHADOW` control its 3D edge.

# Downloadable oTraiL modules

Modules do not ship inside the app APK. The APK contains only the signed catalog manager, loader, public API and in-app worker service. Module packages use the exact extension `.oTrail0`.

- `api/`: API v1 shared by the host, editor, compiler and publisher.
- `src/main/java/in/otrail/`: catalog verification, password gate, package checks, version activation/rollback and isolated app-process lifecycle.
- `mod1/`: GOD source studio implementation, compiled and downloaded separately.
- `releases/`: signed catalog, versioned packages, source archives and compiler packs. No maps, journal data, credentials or private signing keys.
- `plans/`: future module proposals.

A `.oTrail0` file is a ZIP with `module.json`, `classes.dex` and module-specific assets. GitHub `catalog.json` is a signed envelope containing repository/version lists and separately versioned toolchains. The host pins the publisher public key. Every module package is checked against the signed size/SHA256/identity/API before activation and again before loading. Code is read-only before loading, including Android 14+ handling. A previous installed version remains available for rollback.

Settings → Extension modules lets the user refresh, download with progress, enter the install password, activate/open, deactivate or roll back. GOD's first version requires the owner's install password. It generates its own SSH key on the phone; private keys are not embedded in public packages.

Build host first with `. /src/android-build-env/environment.sh` and `./gradlew assembleDebug testDebugUnitTest lintDebug exportGodRuntime`. `scripts/build-god.py prepare` creates tool packs from pinned public dependencies; `package` compiles the separate module, packages source and signs the catalog. Publisher private material is read from `~/.local/share/otrail/` and must stay outside Git. Preserve old version files and catalog entries; bump versions for changes to published packages.

Read mod1/README.md for first-toolchain limits and setup. The first engine supports app Java rebuilds, and explicitly rejects unsupported resource/build-system changes. No external app or remote compiler is used.

package in.otrail.modules;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.content.Intent;
import android.view.View;
import java.io.File;

/** Public ABI shared by the APK host and independently downloaded module DEX packages. */
public interface ModuleV1 {
  int API_VERSION=1;
  interface Host {
    default String photoContext(long capturedMs) throws Exception { throw new UnsupportedOperationException(); }
    default void savePhoto(String metadata) throws Exception { throw new UnsupportedOperationException(); }
    default String photos(long stopId) throws Exception { throw new UnsupportedOperationException(); }
    File packageFile();
    File privateDirectory();
    void startTask(String request) throws Exception;
    void cancelTask();
    String taskStatus();
    String toolchains(boolean refresh) throws Exception;
    String selectedToolchain() throws Exception;
    void selectToolchain(String id) throws Exception;
    void installBuiltApk(File file) throws Exception;
  }
  String id();
  View create(Activity activity,Host host) throws Exception;
  interface Progress {
    void update(String phase,int percent,String log);
    boolean cancelled();
  }
  default void task(File packageFile,File privateDirectory,String request,Progress progress) throws Exception {
    throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Module has no background tasks");
  }
  default void activityResult(int request,int result,Intent data) {}
  default void permissionResult(int request,String[] permissions,int[] grants) {}
  default void resume() {}
  default void pause() {}
  default void close() {}
}

FILE: modules/mod1/README.md

# GOD — downloadable source studio (module ID `mod1`, version 1.0.0)

All screens and work execute inside oTraiL. No Termux, external application, shell, build server or remote compiler. The editor and compiler code are not bundled in the main APK.

## Use

1. On Android 15 or later, update oTraiL to 0.4.0 or later. Android still requires confirmation to install the main APK update.
2. Settings → Extension modules → Refresh versions → GOD → Download & install. Enter the installation password supplied by the owner, then Activate.
3. Tools → Refresh / choose toolchain. Review licenses and download the compatible toolchain. Downloads show sizes/progress and support Wi-Fi/cellular.
4. Project → Download source → Browse files. The editor has file tabs, undo/redo, search, keyword highlighting, save/save-all and recoverable drafts.
5. Import the existing PKCS12 APK signing keystore in Tools. The password/alias and key remain private on this phone, outside source/snapshots/exports. A mismatched certificate is rejected; never uninstall the app to bypass it.
6. Save all & build APK. The dedicated in-app compiler process compiles Java with ECJ, builds DEX with D8, retains verified resources/native libraries, aligns native entries, then signs with apksig. APKs can be exported or installed after identity verification.
7. Generate GitHub SSH key → Download SSH public key. Add it to the GitHub account or repository deploy keys with write access. Configure the repository/branch and test the uploaded key.
8. APKs → Publish APK to GitHub → choose a unique release filename. The Java Git/SSH engine commits `releases/<name>.apk` and its SHA256 sidecar. It does not force-push or use GitHub Releases workflows. Initial Git synchronization can be large because old APKs are stored in the repository.

## First toolchain scope

The initial toolchain rebuilds the app's Java source roots. It preserves compiled resources, manifest, native routing/map libraries and dependency DEX from a verified template. Changes to protected resource/XML/build-system/BRouter source files fail explicitly; they are not silently ignored. New resource files are rejected. Tests and documentation are editable but are not part of the APK compile action. GOD's own source is visible for review; building a new module package is a separate publisher operation.

Toolchains are signed catalog entries with their own versions, download files, hashes, API/host compatibility and source baseline. The Tools selector permits updating a compiler without replacing the APK or editor, within API compatibility. Additional resource-capable engines can be published through that path.

## Storage and integrity

Workspaces, drafts, saved-file backups, five source snapshots, tools, keys and build outputs live under private `modules/data/mod1/`. They are separate from trail databases and map downloads. Installation uses the same package/signing identity; the recorder runs in its existing process. The compiler runs in `:compiler`, the editor in `:modules`. A process crash can interrupt a job, but never replaces the original app or publishes an unfinished APK. APK output becomes visible only after signing completes.

The SSH private key is generated in Android Keystore and is non-exportable. Only its public key can be downloaded. It survives in-place updates; uninstall removes it, so a new key would need registration. Export source ZIPs to retain work outside the app across uninstall. Private signing material is never included in source exports or GitHub commits.

Installation password is a salted PBKDF2 verifier in the signed catalog, not a plaintext credential in the APK. Executable module/tool integrity is authenticated by the publisher signature and checksums. Only trusted signed modules should be activated: they share the app UID and are not a security sandbox.

## Verification limits

The desktop validation runs the same Java compiler engine against real project sources and checks the resulting APK's signature, native-library alignment and retained resources. That does not prove ART/device compatibility. Phone-side module loading, compiler execution, Android Keystore SSH authentication and GitHub publication require device validation; do not treat this first release as device-validated while ADB is disconnected.

FILE: modules/mod1/compiler/in/otrail/extensions/god/compiler/CompilerEngine.java
================================================================================

package in.otrail.extensions.god.compiler;

import in.otrail.modules.*;
import org.eclipse.jdt.core.compiler.CompilationProgress;
import org.eclipse.jdt.core.compiler.batch.BatchCompiler;
import com.android.tools.r8.*;
import com.android.apksig.ApkSigner;
import java.io.*;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.*;
import java.security.*;
import java.security.cert.X509Certificate;
import java.util.*;
import java.util.jar.*;
import java.util.zip.*;
import org.json.*;

/** Real, offline Java → DEX → aligned/signed APK build. No shell, Gradle, server or external app. */
public final class CompilerEngine implements CompilerV1 {
  private static String hash(File file)throws Exception{MessageDigest digest=MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");try(InputStream in=new FileInputStream(file)){byte[] b=new byte[65536];int n;while((n=in.read(b))!=-1)digest.update(b,0,n);}StringBuilder out=new StringBuilder();for(byte b:digest.digest())out.append(String.format(Locale.ROOT,"%02x",b&255));return out.toString();}
  private static byte[] bytes(File file)throws IOException{try(InputStream in=new FileInputStream(file);ByteArrayOutputStream out=new ByteArrayOutputStream()){copy(in,out);return out.toByteArray();}}
  private static void copy(InputStream in,OutputStream out)throws IOException{byte[] b=new byte[65536];int n;while((n=in.read(b))!=-1)out.write(b,0,n);}
  private static void walk(File root,List<File> out,String suffix){File[] list=root.listFiles();if(list==null)return;for(File f:list)if(f.isDirectory())walk(f,out,suffix);else if(f.getName().endsWith(suffix))out.add(f);}
  private static void remove(File f){File[] list=f.listFiles();if(list!=null)for(File child:list)remove(child);f.delete();}
  private static void check(ModuleV1.Progress p)throws IOException{if(p.cancelled())throw new IOException("Build cancelled; original app and prior APKs retained");}
  @Override public void compile(File workspace,File tools,File data,String configuration,ModuleV1.Progress progress)throws Exception{
    JSONObject config=new JSONObject(configuration);StringBuilder log=new StringBuilder("Offline in-app build\n");
    File baselineFile=new File(workspace,".studio-baseline.json");if(!baselineFile.isFile())throw new IOException("Source package has no verified build baseline");
    if(!hash(baselineFile).equals(config.getString("baselineSha256")))throw new SecurityException("Source baseline was modified; download a verified source workspace");
    JSONObject baseline=new JSONObject(new String(bytes(baselineFile),StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    JSONObject immutable=baseline.getJSONObject("protected");

      public void start(int n){}public void beginTask(String name,int count){task=name;total=count;done=0;}public void update(int n){done+=n;long now=System.currentTimeMillis();if(now-updated>1000){updated=now;progress.update(task,total>0?Math.min(80,10+done*60/total):10,log.toString());}}public void endTask(){}public boolean isCancelled(){return progress.cancelled();}public void showDuration(boolean show){}

    }else{
      checkout.getParentFile().mkdirs();git=Git.cloneRepository().setURI(remote).setDirectory(checkout).setNoCheckout(true).setDepth(1).setBranch("refs/heads/"+branch).setBranchesToClone(Collections.singletonList("refs/heads/"+branch)).setTransportConfigCallback(transport).setProgressMonitor(monitor).setTimeout(180).call();
    }

      DirCacheEditor edits=index.editor();add(edits,path,blob,apk.length());add(edits,path+".sha256",checksum,sum.length());edits.finish();

      PersonIdent author=new PersonIdent("GOD on phone","god@otrail.local");commit.setAuthor(author);commit.setCommitter(author);commit.setMessage("Publish phone-built "+releaseName+"\n\nBuilt inside oTraiL GOD; source journal and map data excluded.\n");

      }
      if(!pushed)throw new IOException("No remote branch was updated");progress.update("Published on GitHub",100,"https://github.com/"+repo+"/blob/"+branch+"/"+path+"\nCommit "+next.name()+"\nNo remote force push or GitHub Releases workflow used.\n");
    }
  }
  private static void add(DirCacheEditor edits,String path,ObjectId object,long length){edits.add(new DirCacheEditor.PathEdit(path){public void apply(DirCacheEntry entry){entry.setFileMode(FileMode.REGULAR_FILE);entry.setObjectId(object);entry.setLength(length);}});}
  private static com.jcraft.jsch.Identity identity()throws Exception{
    KeyStore store=KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore");store.load(null);PrivateKey key=(PrivateKey)store.getKey(KEY,null);if(key==null)throw new IOException("Generate and upload the SSH public key in Tools first");RSAPublicKey pub=(RSAPublicKey)store.getCertificate(KEY).getPublicKey();ByteArrayOutputStream bytes=new ByteArrayOutputStream();DataOutputStream out=new DataOutputStream(bytes);put(out,"ssh-rsa".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));put(out,pub.getPublicExponent().toByteArray());put(out,pub.getModulus().toByteArray());final byte[] publicBlob=bytes.toByteArray();
    return new com.jcraft.jsch.Identity(){public String getName(){return "GOD Android Keystore";}public String getAlgName(){return "ssh-rsa";}public byte[] getPublicKeyBlob(){return publicBlob;}public boolean setPassphrase(byte[] pass){return true;}public boolean isEncrypted(){return false;}public void clear(){}
      public byte[] getSignature(byte[] data){return getSignature(data,"rsa-sha2-256");}
      public byte[] getSignature(byte[] data,String algorithm){try{if(!algorithm.equals("rsa-sha2-256")&&!algorithm.equals("rsa-sha2-512"))return null;java.security.Signature signature=java.security.Signature.getInstance(algorithm.equals("rsa-sha2-512")?"SHA512withRSA":"SHA256withRSA");signature.initSign(key);signature.update(data);ByteArrayOutputStream bytes=new ByteArrayOutputStream();DataOutputStream output=new DataOutputStream(bytes);put(output,algorithm.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));put(output,signature.sign());return bytes.toByteArray();}catch(Exception e){return null;}}
    };
  }
  private static void put(DataOutputStream out,byte[] bytes)throws IOException{out.writeInt(bytes.length);out.write(bytes);}
  private static JSONObject json(File file)throws Exception{return new JSONObject(new String(Files.readAllBytes(file.toPath()),StandardCharsets.UTF_8));}
  private static void write(File file,byte[] bytes)throws IOException{Files.write(file.toPath(),bytes);}

package in.otrail.extensions.mod1;
import android.security.keystore.*;
import java.io.*;
import java.math.BigInteger;
import java.security.*;
import java.security.interfaces.RSAPublicKey;
import java.util.Base64;

final class GitKeys {
  static final String ALIAS="otrail.god.github.ssh";
  static File generate(File data)throws Exception{
    KeyStore store=KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore");store.load(null);
    if(!store.containsAlias(ALIAS)){
      KeyPairGenerator generator=KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("RSA","AndroidKeyStore");
      generator.initialize(new KeyGenParameterSpec.Builder(ALIAS,KeyProperties.PURPOSE_SIGN).setKeySize(3072).setDigests(KeyProperties.DIGEST_SHA256,KeyProperties.DIGEST_SHA512).setSignaturePaddings(KeyProperties.SIGNATURE_PADDING_RSA_PKCS1).build());generator.generateKeyPair();
    }
    RSAPublicKey key=(RSAPublicKey)store.getCertificate(ALIAS).getPublicKey();ByteArrayOutputStream bytes=new ByteArrayOutputStream();DataOutputStream out=new DataOutputStream(bytes);put(out,"ssh-rsa".getBytes("UTF-8"));put(out,key.getPublicExponent().toByteArray());put(out,key.getModulus().toByteArray());
    File pub=new File(data,"GOD-github.pub");StudioFiles.write(pub,("ssh-rsa "+Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(bytes.toByteArray())+" oTraiL-GOD\n").getBytes("UTF-8"));return pub;
  }
  private static void put(DataOutputStream out,byte[] data)throws IOException{out.writeInt(data.length);out.write(data);}
}

  private JSONObject obj(Object... pairs)throws JSONException{JSONObject j=new JSONObject();for(int i=0;i<pairs.length;i+=2)j.put((String)pairs[i],pairs[i+1]);return j;}
  private interface Work {void run()throws Exception;}
  private void work(Work work){io.execute(()->{try{work.run();}catch(Exception e){error(e);}});}
  private String asset(String name)throws Exception{try(ZipFile zip=new ZipFile(host.packageFile());InputStream in=zip.getInputStream(zip.getEntry(name))){return new String(read(in,300000),StandardCharsets.UTF_8);}}

  private void compactButtons(LinearLayout panel){
    if(activity.getResources().getConfiguration().orientation!=android.content.res.Configuration.ORIENTATION_LANDSCAPE)return;
    ArrayList<View> views=new ArrayList<>();for(int i=0;i<panel.getChildCount();i++)views.add(panel.getChildAt(i));panel.removeAllViews();
    LinearLayout buttons=null;int column=0;
    for(View view:views){
      if(view instanceof Button&&!(view instanceof android.widget.CompoundButton)){
        if(buttons==null||column==3){buttons=row();panel.addView(buttons,new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(-1,-2));column=0;}
        LinearLayout.LayoutParams p=new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(0,dp(48),1);p.setMargins(dp(3),dp(3),dp(3),dp(3));buttons.addView(view,p);column++;
      }else{if(buttons!=null)while(column++<3)buttons.addView(new View(activity),new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(0,dp(48),1));buttons=null;column=0;panel.addView(view);}
    }
    if(buttons!=null)while(column++<3)buttons.addView(new View(activity),new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(0,dp(48),1));
  }

  private void browse(){work(()->{

  private void openFile(String path){
    synchronized(buffers){if(buffers.containsKey(path)){current=path;show("Editor");return;}}
    work(()->{final String project=StudioFiles.project(host.privateDirectory()).getCanonicalPath();
      if(!draftProject.isEmpty()&&!draftProject.equals(project))throw new IOException("Close saved editor tabs before switching source workspaces");
      final String text=call(obj("action","read","path",path)).getString("text");ui(()->{draftProject=project;Buffer b=new Buffer();b.text=b.saved=text;synchronized(buffers){buffers.put(path,b);}current=path;show("Editor");});});
  }
  private void editorScreen(){
    HorizontalScrollView tabs=new HorizontalScrollView(activity);fileTabs=row();tabs.addView(fileTabs);content.addView(tabs);
    synchronized(buffers){for(Map.Entry<String,Buffer> entry:buffers.entrySet()){String path=entry.getKey();Buffer b=entry.getValue();b.button=button(shortName(path)+(b.dirty()?" *":""),()->{current=path;show("Editor");});fileTabs.addView(b.button);}}
    content.addView(label(current.isEmpty()?"Open a file from Project":current,12));
    LinearLayout actions=new LinearLayout(activity);actions.setOrientation(1);
    actions.addView(button("Files",this::browse));actions.addView(button("Save",()->work(()->saveOne(current))));actions.addView(button("Save all",()->work(()->saveAllNetwork())));
    actions.addView(button("Undo",()->undo(false)));actions.addView(button("Redo",()->undo(true)));actions.addView(button("Find",this::find));actions.addView(button("Close file",this::closeFile));compactButtons(actions);content.addView(actions);
    editor=new EditText(activity);editor.setTextColor(TEXT);editor.setBackgroundColor(0xff181827);editor.setTextSize(14);editor.setTypeface(Typeface.MONOSPACE);editor.setGravity(Gravity.TOP|Gravity.START);editor.setSingleLine(false);editor.setHorizontallyScrolling(true);editor.setInputType(android.text.InputType.TYPE_CLASS_TEXT|android.text.InputType.TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_MULTI_LINE|android.text.InputType.TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_NO_SUGGESTIONS);
    Buffer b=buffers.get(current);editor.setText(b==null?"":b.text);editor.setEnabled(b!=null);content.addView(editor,new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(-1,0,1));highlight();
    editor.addTextChangedListener(new SimpleWatcher(){
      public void beforeTextChanged(CharSequence s,int start,int count,int after){Buffer buffer=buffers.get(current);if(buffer==null||suppress)return;long now=System.currentTimeMillis();if(now-buffer.undoTime>700){buffer.undo.push(s.toString());while(buffer.undo.size()>20)buffer.undo.removeLast();buffer.undoTime=now;}buffer.redo.clear();}
      public void afterTextChanged(Editable text){Buffer buffer=buffers.get(current);if(buffer==null)return;buffer.text=text.toString();if(buffer.button!=null)buffer.button.setText(shortName(current)+(buffer.dirty()?" *":""));highlight();handler.removeCallbacks(draftSave);handler.postDelayed(draftSave,300);}
    });
  }
  private String shortName(String path){return path.substring(path.lastIndexOf('/')+1);}
  private void highlight(){if(editor==null||editor.length()>100000)return;Editable text=editor.getText();for(ForegroundColorSpan span:text.getSpans(0,text.length(),ForegroundColorSpan.class))text.removeSpan(span);
    Matcher matcher=Pattern.compile("\\b(class|public|private|protected|static|final|void|return|if|else|new|import|package|int|long|boolean|record|extends|implements|try|catch|throw)\\b").matcher(text);
    while(matcher.find())text.setSpan(new ForegroundColorSpan(0xffff40d0),matcher.start(),matcher.end(),Spanned.SPAN_EXCLUSIVE_EXCLUSIVE);
  }
  private void undo(boolean redo){Buffer b=buffers.get(current);if(b==null)return;Deque<String> from=redo?b.redo:b.undo,to=redo?b.undo:b.redo;if(from.isEmpty())return;to.push(b.text);suppress=true;editor.setText(from.pop());suppress=false;}
  private void find(){if(editor==null)return;EditText query=new EditText(activity);new AlertDialog.Builder(activity).setTitle("Find in file").setView(query).setPositiveButton("Find",(d,w)->{String needle=query.getText().toString();int at=editor.getText().toString().indexOf(needle,Math.max(0,editor.getSelectionEnd()));if(at<0)at=editor.getText().toString().indexOf(needle);if(at>=0){editor.requestFocus();editor.setSelection(at,at+needle.length());}else status.setText("Text not found");}).setNegativeButton("Cancel",null).show();}
  private void closeFile(){Buffer b=buffers.get(current);if(b==null)return;final String path=current;Runnable close=()->{buffers.remove(path);if(buffers.isEmpty())draftProject="";current=buffers.isEmpty()?"":buffers.keySet().iterator().next();show("Editor");};
    if(b.dirty())new AlertDialog.Builder(activity).setTitle("Unsaved changes").setMessage(path).setPositiveButton("Save & close",(d,w)->work(()->{saveOne(path);ui(close);})).setNeutralButton("Discard",(d,w)->close.run()).setNegativeButton("Cancel",null).show();else close.run();
  }
  private void saveOne(String path)throws Exception{final Buffer b;final String text;synchronized(buffers){b=buffers.get(path);if(b==null||!b.dirty())return;text=b.text;}if(!draftProject.isEmpty()&&!draftProject.equals(StudioFiles.project(host.privateDirectory()).getCanonicalPath()))throw new IOException("This draft belongs to another source workspace; reopen that version before saving");call(obj("action","write","path",path,"text",text));ui(()->{b.saved=text;if(b.button!=null)b.button.setText(shortName(path)+(b.dirty()?" *":""));status.setText("Saved "+path);saveDrafts();});}
  private void saveAllNetwork()throws Exception{List<String> paths;synchronized(buffers){paths=new ArrayList<>(buffers.keySet());}for(String path:paths)saveOne(path);}
  private void openError(){String output=state.optString("log");Matcher m=Pattern.compile("([^\\s:]+\\.java):(\\d+):").matcher(output);if(m.find()){String path=m.group(1);int index=path.indexOf("/app/");if(index>=0)path=path.substring(index+1);else{index=path.indexOf("/modules/");if(index>=0)path=path.substring(index+1);}openFile(path);}else status.setText("No Java error location in current log");}
  private void saveDrafts(){if(host==null)return;try{JSONObject root=new JSONObject();JSONArray files=new JSONArray();synchronized(buffers){for(Map.Entry<String,Buffer> e:buffers.entrySet())files.put(obj("path",e.getKey(),"text",e.getValue().text,"saved",e.getValue().saved));}root.put("files",files).put("current",current).put("project",draftProject);android.util.AtomicFile atomic=new android.util.AtomicFile(new File(host.privateDirectory(),"drafts.json"));FileOutputStream out=atomic.startWrite();try{out.write(root.toString().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));atomic.finishWrite(out);}catch(Exception e){atomic.failWrite(out);throw e;}}catch(Exception e){error(e);}}
  private void restoreDrafts()throws Exception{File file=new File(host.privateDirectory(),"drafts.json");if(!file.isFile()&&!new File(file.getPath()+".bak").isFile())return;JSONObject data;try(InputStream in=new android.util.AtomicFile(file).openRead()){data=new JSONObject(new String(read(in,64000000),StandardCharsets.UTF_8));}JSONArray files=data.getJSONArray("files");for(int i=0;i<files.length();i++){JSONObject f=files.getJSONObject(i);Buffer b=new Buffer();b.text=f.getString("text");b.saved=f.getString("saved");buffers.put(f.getString("path"),b);}current=data.optString("current","");draftProject=data.optString("project","");}
  private JSONObject call(JSONObject request)throws Exception{
    String action=request.getString("action");File data=host.privateDirectory();
    if(action.equals("status")){
      JSONObject result=new JSONObject(host.taskStatus());
      try{result.put("project",StudioFiles.project(data).getPath());}catch(Exception ignored){}
      result.put("freeBytes",data.getUsableSpace()).put("signingConfigured",new File(data,"signing.keystore").isFile()).put("toolsReady",new File(data,"tools/ready.json").isFile());
      JSONArray outputs=new JSONArray();File[] files=new File(data,"outputs").listFiles();if(files!=null){Arrays.sort(files,Comparator.comparing(File::getName).reversed());for(File f:files)if(f.getName().endsWith(".apk"))outputs.put(obj("name",f.getName(),"size",f.length()));}return result.put("outputs",outputs);
    }
    if(action.equals("cancel")){host.cancelTask();return obj("ok",true);}
    if(action.equals("source")||action.equals("setup")||action.equals("build")||action.startsWith("github")){
      if(new JSONObject(host.taskStatus()).optBoolean("busy"))throw new IOException("Another tool task is running");
      if(action.equals("source")&&!buffers.isEmpty())throw new IOException("Save and close editor tabs before selecting a source workspace");
      host.startTask(request.toString());return obj("ok",true);
    }
    if(action.equals("signing")){
      byte[] key=Base64.getDecoder().decode(request.getString("keystore"));if(key.length>200000)throw new IOException("Keystore too large");
      StudioFiles.write(new File(data,"signing.keystore"),key);StudioFiles.write(new File(data,"signing.json"),obj("alias",request.getString("alias"),"password",request.getString("password"),"keyPassword",request.getString("keyPassword")).toString().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));return obj("ok",true);
    }
    File project=StudioFiles.project(data);
    if(action.equals("files")){JSONArray files=new JSONArray();for(File f:StudioFiles.files(project))files.put(StudioFiles.relative(project,f));return obj("files",files);}
    if(action.equals("read"))return obj("text",new String(StudioFiles.read(StudioFiles.safe(project,request.getString("path")),500000),StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    if(action.equals("write")){
      if(new JSONObject(host.taskStatus()).optBoolean("busy"))throw new IOException("Wait for the current tool task before saving");
      File target=StudioFiles.safe(project,request.getString("path"));byte[] text=request.getString("text").getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);if(text.length>500000)throw new IOException("File exceeds editor size limit");
      if(target.isFile()){File backup=new File(data,"backups/"+System.currentTimeMillis()+"-"+target.getName());backup.getParentFile().mkdirs();java.nio.file.Files.copy(target.toPath(),backup.toPath(),java.nio.file.StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);}StudioFiles.write(target,text);return obj("ok",true);
    }
    if(action.equals("export")){File snapshot=StudioFiles.snapshot(project,data),output=new File(data,"outputs/oTraiL-source-"+System.currentTimeMillis()+".zip");output.getParentFile().mkdirs();java.nio.file.Files.copy(snapshot.toPath(),output.toPath());return obj("name",output.getName());}
    throw new IOException("Unknown in-app operation");
  }
  private void download(String name,boolean install,boolean export)throws Exception{
    if(!name.matches("oTraiL-(phone-[0-9-]+\\.apk|source-[0-9]+\\.zip)"))throw new IOException("Invalid output filename");
    File target=new File(host.privateDirectory(),"outputs/"+name);if(!target.isFile())throw new IOException("Build output not found");
    if(install)ui(()->{try{host.installBuiltApk(target);}catch(Exception e){error(e);}});
    if(export){exportFile=target;exportMime=name.endsWith(".apk")?"application/vnd.android.package-archive":"application/zip";ui(()->activity.startActivityForResult(new Intent(Intent.ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT).setType(exportMime).putExtra(Intent.EXTRA_TITLE,name).addCategory(Intent.CATEGORY_OPENABLE),EXPORT));}
  }
  @Override public void task(File packageFile,File privateDirectory,String request,Progress progress)throws Exception{StudioTasks.run(packageFile,privateDirectory,request,progress);}
  @Override public void activityResult(int request,int result,Intent data){if(result!=Activity.RESULT_OK||data==null||data.getData()==null)return;final Uri uri=data.getData();
    if(request==EXPORT&&exportFile!=null){final File file=exportFile;work(()->{try(InputStream in=new FileInputStream(file);OutputStream out=activity.getContentResolver().openOutputStream(uri)){byte[] b=new byte[32768];int n;while((n=in.read(b))!=-1)out.write(b,0,n);}ui(()->status.setText("Saved "+file.getName()));});}
    if(request==KEYSTORE){LinearLayout form=new LinearLayout(activity);form.setOrientation(1);EditText alias=new EditText(activity);alias.setHint("Key alias (for example androiddebugkey)");EditText password=new EditText(activity);password.setHint("Store password");password.setInputType(129);EditText keyPassword=new EditText(activity);keyPassword.setHint("Key password (blank = store password)");keyPassword.setInputType(129);form.addView(alias);form.addView(password);form.addView(keyPassword);
      new AlertDialog.Builder(activity).setTitle("Import signing keystore").setView(form).setPositiveButton("Import privately",(d,w)->{final String a=alias.getText().toString(),p=password.getText().toString(),kp=keyPassword.getText().toString();work(()->{byte[] key;try(InputStream in=activity.getContentResolver().openInputStream(uri)){key=read(in,200000);}call(obj("action","signing","keystore",Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(key),"alias",a,"password",p,"keyPassword",kp.isEmpty()?p:kp));ui(()->status.setText("Signing keystore imported privately on this phone"));});}).setNegativeButton("Cancel",null).show();
    }
  }
  private byte[] read(InputStream in,int limit)throws IOException{ByteArrayOutputStream out=new ByteArrayOutputStream();byte[] b=new byte[16384];int n;while((n=in.read(b))!=-1){if(out.size()+n>limit)throw new IOException("File too large");out.write(b,0,n);}return out.toByteArray();}
  @Override public void resume(){running=true;handler.removeCallbacks(poll);handler.post(poll);}
  @Override public void pause(){running=false;handler.removeCallbacks(poll);handler.removeCallbacks(draftSave);saveDrafts();}
  @Override public void close(){pause();closed=true;io.shutdownNow();}
  private static class SimpleWatcher implements TextWatcher{public void beforeTextChanged(CharSequence s,int st,int c,int a){}public void onTextChanged(CharSequence s,int st,int before,int count){}public void afterTextChanged(Editable e){}}
}

package in.otrail.extensions.mod1;

import java.io.*;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.*;
import java.security.MessageDigest;
import java.util.*;
import java.util.zip.*;
import org.json.*;

final class StudioFiles {
  static byte[] read(File f,int limit)throws IOException{try(InputStream in=new FileInputStream(f)){return read(in,limit);}}
  static byte[] read(InputStream in,int limit)throws IOException{ByteArrayOutputStream out=new ByteArrayOutputStream();byte[] b=new byte[32768];int n;while((n=in.read(b))!=-1){if(out.size()+n>limit)throw new IOException("File exceeds size limit");out.write(b,0,n);}return out.toByteArray();}
  static JSONObject json(File f)throws Exception{return new JSONObject(new String(read(f,2000000),StandardCharsets.UTF_8));}
  static void write(File f,byte[] bytes)throws IOException{f.getParentFile().mkdirs();File part=new File(f.getPath()+".part");try(FileOutputStream out=new FileOutputStream(part)){out.write(bytes);out.getFD().sync();}Files.move(part.toPath(),f.toPath(),StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);}
  static File project(File data)throws Exception{File f=new File(json(new File(data,"project.json")).getString("path")).getCanonicalFile();File parent=new File(data,"projects").getCanonicalFile();if(!f.getPath().startsWith(parent.getPath()+File.separator)||!f.isDirectory())throw new IOException("Download a source version first");return f;}
  static File safe(File root,String relative)throws IOException{if(relative.isEmpty()||relative.contains("\\"))throw new IOException("Invalid workspace path");File f=new File(root,relative).getCanonicalFile();if(!f.getPath().startsWith(root.getCanonicalPath()+File.separator))throw new IOException("Path outside project");for(String part:relative.split("/"))if(part.equals(".git")||part.equals("build")||part.equals(".gradle"))throw new IOException("Generated files are not editable");return f;}
  static List<File> files(File root)throws IOException{List<File> out=new ArrayList<>();walk(root,root,out);return out;}
  private static void walk(File root,File dir,List<File> out)throws IOException{File[] files=dir.listFiles();if(files==null)return;for(File f:files){if(Files.isSymbolicLink(f.toPath()))continue;if(f.isDirectory()){if(!Arrays.asList("build",".gradle",".git","releases").contains(f.getName()))walk(root,f,out);}else if(f.length()<500000)out.add(f);if(out.size()>25000)throw new IOException("Too many project files");}}
  static String relative(File root,File f){return root.toURI().relativize(f.toURI()).getPath();}
  static String sha(File f)throws Exception{MessageDigest d=MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");try(InputStream in=new FileInputStream(f)){byte[] b=new byte[65536];int n;while((n=in.read(b))!=-1)d.update(b,0,n);}StringBuilder out=new StringBuilder();for(byte b:d.digest())out.append(String.format(Locale.ROOT,"%02x",b&255));return out.toString();}
  static File snapshot(File root,File data)throws Exception{File dest=new File(data,"snapshots/source-"+System.currentTimeMillis()+".zip");dest.getParentFile().mkdirs();try(ZipOutputStream zip=new ZipOutputStream(new FileOutputStream(dest))){for(File f:files(root)){zip.putNextEntry(new ZipEntry(relative(root,f)));try(InputStream in=new FileInputStream(f)){byte[] b=new byte[32768];int n;while((n=in.read(b))!=-1)zip.write(b,0,n);}zip.closeEntry();}}File[] old=dest.getParentFile().listFiles();if(old!=null){Arrays.sort(old,Comparator.comparing(File::getName));for(int i=0;i<old.length-5;i++)old[i].delete();}return dest;}
  static void unzip(File archive,File destination)throws Exception{destination.mkdirs();long total=0;int count=0;Set<String> names=new HashSet<>();try(ZipInputStream zip=new ZipInputStream(new FileInputStream(archive))){ZipEntry e;byte[] b=new byte[32768];while((e=zip.getNextEntry())!=null){if(++count>30000||!names.add(e.getName()))throw new IOException("Invalid archive entries");File target=safe(destination,e.getName());if(e.isDirectory()){target.mkdirs();continue;}target.getParentFile().mkdirs();try(FileOutputStream out=new FileOutputStream(target)){if((target.getName().endsWith(".dex")||target.getName().equals("compiler.jar")||target.getName().equals("publisher.jar"))&&!target.setReadOnly())throw new IOException("Cannot protect compiler code");int n;while((n=zip.read(b))!=-1){total+=n;if(total>250000000)throw new IOException("Archive exceeds unpacked size limit");out.write(b,0,n);}}}}}
  static void remove(File file){File[] children=file.listFiles();if(children!=null)for(File f:children)remove(f);file.delete();}
}
